title: Private deploy networking - VPC peering / DNS / TLS / egress incident notes
content:
Summary:
- Customer on private deployment reported intermittent 502s from control-plane -> worker gateway when pulling model artifacts and during healthchecks. Issue surfaced after VPC peering change on 2025-08-11 (peer added to frankfurt region).
- Symptoms: successful model load sometimes, then TLS handshake failures, then DNS NXDOMAIN for internal service name, then normal again. Flaky but reproducible with load.

Timeline notes (local repro attempts):
- 2025-08-12 09:10: initial triage with Noah - reproduced failing curl from control-plane to worker-gateway (10.40.x.x).
- 2025-08-12 09:22: added tcpdump on worker-gateway NIC eth0 while reproducing.
- 2025-08-12 09:30: observed RSTs from intermediate firewall for some flows, not all.

Commands tried / outputs (copied snippets):
- dig against internal service (from control-plane pod):
  $ dig +short worker-gateway.internal.pd
  (when healthy) -> 10.40.12.8
  (when failing) -> ;; connection timed out; no servers

- curl with verbose TLS:
  $ curl -v https://worker-gateway.internal.pd:8443/health
  * Rebuilt URL to: https://worker-gateway.internal.pd:8443/health
  *   Trying 10.40.12.8...
  * Connected to worker-gateway.internal.pd (10.40.12.8) port 8443 (#0)
  * schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012) - The revocation function was unable to check revocation for the certificate.
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012)

- openssl s_client test (from control-plane VM):
  $ openssl s_client -connect 10.40.12.8:8443 -servername worker-gateway.internal.pd -tls1_2
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139832...:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:
  ---
  no peer certificate available
  ---
  SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 310 bytes

- tcpdump (filtered) observed pattern: initial SYN,SYN-ACK then client TLS ClientHello then immediate RST from 10.40.0.1 (firewall) for ~40% of attempts. For other attempts there is full handshake and GET/200.

- ip route / iptables checks on worker-gateway + control-plane: routing table looks correct. No egress proxy configured on control-plane.

Hypotheses / notes:
- Hypothesis A: Firewall/NAT gateway on the peered VPC intermittently rejects TLS ClientHello packets when SNI matches certain name or when connection rate exceeds threshold -> causes RST. Observed RST from 10.40.0.1 aligns (edge NAT IP).
- Hypothesis B: DNS caching + stale SRV/ALIAS records causing requests to hit a decommissioned AZ instance (no cert) -> explains "no peer certificate" with handshake failure. But dig NXDOMAIN seen sometimes too, suggesting resolver instability rather than DNS records being wrong.
- Hypothesis C: MTU or fragmentation issue introduced by peering path -> fragmented TLS ClientHello dropped by middlebox. We saw smaller packet sizes on success vs failing attempts (need to confirm).
- Hypothesis D: TLS client certificate verification failing because CRL/OCSP fetching blocked egress -> schannel error about revocation check suggests client attempted revocation check and couldn't reach OCSP; but openssl shows handshake failure earlier. Could be a red herring (schannel-specific).

Local experiments to validate hypotheses:
- Reproduced with curl --http2 disabled and curl --header "Host: worker-gateway.internal.pd" to force SNI variations: failure rate unchanged. Suggests SNI not the immediate trigger.
- Forced MTU 1400 on control-plane interface -> failure rate dropped to ~5% in 200 attempts. When restored to default MTU 1500, failure ~38%. That strongly points to MTU/fragmentation path issue.
- Ran traceroute and tracepath: tracepath shows a hop reducing MTU on the path (next hop PMTU 1400). Need to map which device.

Notes from cloud provider peering config:
- Provider peering had recently had route-table change to enable transitive routing between tenants (accidental). There is a managed middlebox in the provider fabric that enforces deep-packet inspection with strict MTU enforcement.
- Provider confirms they saw ICMP frag-needed from an inline device for some flows in the timeframe.

Immediate mitigations applied (temporary):
- Set MTU to 1400 on affected control-plane and worker-gateway hosts (rolling) -> reduced errors significantly for the customer.
- Added iptables rule to clamp MSS for TCP SYN (clamp-mss) to 1360 on control-plane as additional mitigation.

Longer-term actions / TODOs:
- (Owner: Priya) Coordinate with cloud provider network team to identify the exact device and reason for MTU reduction and remove accidental transitive config.
- (Owner: Noah) Add automated PMTU check to private-deploy healthchecks (flag when PMTU < 1500).
- (Owner: Maya) Update runbook: include quick mitigation steps (clamp-mss, set MTU, validate with tracepath).
- Add monitoring: capture rate of "no peer certificate" + TLS handshake failures + DNS NXDOMAIN spikes and correlate with MTU change events.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did provider change introduce visible PMTU change only after peering update? Is there an ACL that triggers DPI which drops fragments?
- Is ocsp/crl egress required for our internal TLS client path? If yes, needs allowlist on peering egress rules.
- Should we default private-deploy hosts to 1400 MTU in regions where provider-managed middleboxes are common? Tradeoffs: performance vs stability.

Logs attached in runbook (linked artifact) - raw tcpdump + pcap saved in secure bucket (link in Confluence). Will upload filtered pcap to JIRA ticket for infra network team.

Quick repro steps for SRE when debugging locally:
1) from control-plane pod: dig +short worker-gateway.internal.pd repeatedly (watch for NXDOMAIN)
2) curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://worker-gateway.internal.pd:8443/health (note schannel/openssl output)
3) tracepath -n worker-gateway.internal.pd (look for PMTU changes)
4) sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400 ; rerun tests to verify drop in failure rate
5) tcptrace/tcpdump capture: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.40.12.8 and look for SYN/ClientHello vs RST patterns

Scratchpad / quick commands I ran locally while triaging:
- sudo ip link show ; sudo ip -6 addr ; ip route show table all
- sudo sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 (enabled to see recovery behavior)
- sudo iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

Notes to self: capture full pcap for provider (pcap currently ~120MB filtered). Keep one good and one bad session with timings.

Status: mitigation (MTU clamp) in place customer-facing; provider engaged; next sync scheduled 2025-08-15 with provider network team.

-- Priya
